patch_description: The best prior program (score 3412.97, makespan 292) used beam search with randomized restarts followed by time-budgeted simulated annealing with insertion/swap moves and greedy intensification. The current program (2976) regressed to randomized greedy. I restore the superior approach and add adaptive beam width: wide beam early in each beam-search expansion (where pruning error compounds most) and narrower later, as recommended. This evaluates actual makespan cost at each step, avoiding poor heuristics, and the annealing phase escapes local minima.
